launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-c3-webserver
description: The phone's local web server, as an APK, a native Kotlin / Compose app (#1682) whose Rust core starts the shared fleet web server (ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/fleet-webserver, the Linux my-webserver UI bundled verbatim) in-process on 8002, rooted at /storage/emulated/0 and nothing else, and draws the app shell natively: five bottom tabs Pages, API, Home, SSHd and ADB Shell, Configs behind the top bar's gear (the same pages the server's own web shell serves on /__app__/). A tapped link offers Open in browser or Open embedded (build.json::links). The SuperApp's About, Logcat and Diagnose are served on 8003, and a private DNS (udp 5354) answers termux.app, nix.app, emulated.app and cloud.app.
_doc: WHY NATIVE, AND WHERE THE KOTLIN IS (#1682 P1). The app was a hand-written Kotlin shell (#712 replaced it by a Tauri 2 webview app), then the owner moved it to a native Kotlin / Compose app over the Rust core: core/ is a Rust cdylib (four JNI entry points plus the nav declaration, core/src/lib.rs; the Android calls the server crate needs, core/src/bridge.rs) that calls server/'s start() on threads of the app's own process, exactly as before; the Compose UI (src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/.../cloudwebserver, build.json::native.kotlin) draws the fleet bars and reads the server's own loopback admin API (/__app__/api/...). The web shell server/ui/shell.html is still served on /__app__/ (cloud-browser can open it), and test/test-c3-webserver-native.sh holds the native pages equal to it (routes, pages, actions, statuses) and refuses Tauri coming back. The file view at / is NOT written here: it is the Linux my-webserver frontend, bundled at build time by ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/fleet-webserver from a hash-checked mirror of cloud-u-linux/da_my-webserver/src (one source of truth, no copy in this app); this app adds only its own pages under /__app__/.

native._doc: #1682 P1 THE one declaration of how the APK is built, now that the UI is native Kotlin / Compose and Tauri is gone. crate_dir is the Rust core (a cdylib named lib_name, which the Kotlin app loads with System.loadLibrary; four JNI entry points in core/src/lib.rs, the Android calls in core/src/bridge.rs); server_crate is the library it links and starts, unchanged; android_project is the gradle project (its path is the Tauri-era one because other apps read its AndroidManifest.xml there); targets maps each Android ABI to the Rust triple build.sh cross-compiles with the NDK clang (rust) and the clang target prefix (clang). build.sh builds the core in cargo's release profile, copies the .so into android_project/app/src/main/jniLibs/<abi>/ (gitignored) and runs gradle assembleRelease; the APK is re-signed with the shared key either way. The Compose UI reads the server's own loopback admin API (/__app__/api/..., runtime.port): the same routes the web shell (server/ui/shell.html, still served) reads, so the HTTP surface and every bind are exactly as before.

kotlin._doc: The app's own Kotlin (test/test-c3-webserver-native.sh holds it): the four Android components the manifest declares plus the Compose UI. Every .kt/.java of the app lives under dir; a Kotlin/Java file anywhere else in the app, a Tauri file coming back (tauri.conf.json, a tauri dependency, a WryActivity/TauriActivity reference) or a *.gradle.kts not in build_scripts fails.

owner_dirs._doc: #1682 P2b the ADB owner side: exactly one of the two is compiled (app/build.gradle.kts adbOwnerSide from adb-owner.json). dormant = the shipped inactive stand-in (AdbOwnerSide.active = false), owner = the real owner, built by the CI verify.

ui._doc: #1682 P1 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl) of the native app, the same five bottom tabs the web shell (server/ui/shell.html, app.rs ROUTES) draws: Pages, API, Home, SSHd, ADB Shell; Configs is behind the top bar's gear (the fleet-default entry, #1677). Pages has the #1677 sub-pages All | File Explorer | Pages (id browser: a page id is unique, N12) over build.json::roots; API has Topology then the declared api sub-pages of build.json::subpages (same ids and labels, test-c3-webserver-native.sh holds them equal); Configs starts General | Perms | About (configs-tabs T1) and carries the web shell's own Configs pages (Server: the switches, serving and config; Device: the device report the web Configs > About showed; Engines; Links), then libs:ui-nav-bars FleetConfigsExtensions.withTail appends the fleet tail | Agents, Perms, Logcat, X-Ray App, About. Every icon is a libs:ui-icons name.

power._doc: #1502 THE TWO MASTER CONTROLS (Home and Configs > General, server/src/power.rs, KeepAliveService.kt). Server ON/OFF: OFF stops every CONTENT listener (diagnostics, DNS, mesh listener, every Repos site, sshd) and makes the drive answer 503 for everything but /__app__; the ADMIN surface (:8002 /__app__ + /api/power, `admin` true in every row) is never unbound, so the web UI can always switch the server back on; ON starts them and the Repos sites enabled. Keep alive ON/OFF (default OFF): OFF means no foreground service, no sticky restart, no boot receiver and no scheduled wake, so the server runs while the app process does and nothing revives it; ON runs the foreground service (notification with a Stop action) and the boot autostart, only while Server is ON. `store` is read by both the Rust crate and the Kotlin glue. `matrix` is the decision table; power.rs::plan is held equal to it by a test. Any other app's start request (SuperApp wake, MCP phone tools, log export, Cloud Browser) is honoured by the service only in the one row where `service` is true. `off_url` is the Tauri-bundled page shown while the server is off (a backstop only: the web UI at /__app__ stays up while OFF and is the primary way back to ON).

runtime._doc: Baked into BuildConfig by app/build.gradle and passed to the server positionally as <port> <root>. Both listeners bind 127.0.0.1 only and refuse every other peer: `port` serves the emulated drive (serve_root) and nothing else, `diag.port` serves the fleet-diagnostics page and no files. Option 37.1: 8002, because 127.0.0.1:8000 and :8001 are the two Cloud Terminals' own my-webserver (ac_cloud-termux, ac_cloud-nix-on-droid build.json::runtime.webserver). Every app's localhost ports live under runtime; test/test-localhost-ports.sh fails when two apps declare the same one.

mesh._doc: #1490 THE MESH LISTENER: the fleet's log exports, routed onto the mesh. It binds the phone's own mesh address ONLY (never 0.0.0.0, never loopback, never a public address): `bind` is resolved at build time by server/build.rs from `profile_from` (the first IPv4 of that WireGuard profile's address, declared once in the SuperApp), and the listener refuses to start unless it lies inside `cidrs`; it answers only peers from those subnets AND only with the fleet bearer (the token the SuperApp mints, read through its fleet provider) on every path. While the tunnel is down the address does not exist, the bind fails and is retried every `retry_s` seconds. `/logs/<app>` calls that app's <package>.logexport provider (libs:log-export) and relays its JSON; `/logs` lists the apps. Nothing here names an app: the list is the fleet manifest.
mesh._doc_ipc_route: #1495/#1580 the UNIFIED holder prefix: /ipc/<app>/<route> fronts every fleet app's on-device IPC through one gateway with centralized per-peer, per-route ACL read from data/api-ipc-map.json (acl_scopes, peers, ipc_registry). #1580 removed the per-app /browser and /shell mesh endpoints in favour of it; the per-app /logs route below is still served too (kept until its mesh_page row moves to the gateway).
mesh._doc_no_wake: #1502 a /logs/<app> call starts that app (ContentResolver.call on its provider). Cloud Account must never be woken in the background and Cloud Store only with auto-update on over Wi-Fi, so these two answer 403 here instead.

api._doc: #1490 the data of the API tab's sub-pages (#1495: the FIRST, MCP, is the MCP tool catalogue of all our APIs and MCP servers, GENERATED by data/gen_mcp_catalogue.py into data/mcp-catalogue.json from the containers' build.json files, mcp-policy.json, api-renames.json and the cloudy-c3-api route hierarchy), all read from declarations that already exist (`file#dotted.path` from the repo root, resolved by server/build.rs): the public and mesh URLs of the fleet services (Cloud Account's fleet_endpoints), the per-app debug ports (the debug-port table every app's debug-api.json slice is cut from), and the app roster with its engines (the fleet manifest). `ipc` is the template of each app's IPC endpoints, `{package}` being the app's package: derived, never typed per app.

debug_routes.what: the app's own debug routes, fleet bearer on everything but ping (libs:devtools AppDebugServer)

ipc.what: the app's recent logcat and crash ring as JSON (libs:log-export); Cloud-Webserver serves it on the mesh as /logs/<app>
the mesh handshake: the fleet token and the fleet IPC door (libs:devtools)
the setup contract of the stores the app declares (libs:fleetconfig-model)
the visibility marker that makes every member visible to its siblings

ssh_doors._doc: THE ONE declaration of the fleet's SSH doors, read by server/src/door.rs and drawn by the SSHd tab (the Files tab's replacement, #1565) and the Server card. HOSTING MODEL (owner decision): exactly three apps may host an sshd, each on its own port: this webserver (ON by default, `hosted`), Cloud Terminal Termux and Cloud Terminal Nix-on-Droid (both OFF by default, `default_on` false). The SuperApp hosts no sshd and has no sshd page or row. The supervised door is the nix-on-droid mesh sshd (real OpenSSH, key auth, the door cloud-superapp-mcp already dials). Keep alive (or the door's own switch) makes this app ask that app to start it through its exported, CONSTELLATION_DATA-guarded MeshSshdService (ac_cloud-nix-on-droid build.json::mesh_sshd.control), at the keep-alive service's start (so at boot) and on a switch change; the sshd, its port, host key and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys stay in that app's uid and home. Every `<key>_from` is `file#dotted.path` from the repo root and server/build.rs resolves it into `<key>`: no port, package, action name or bind is written twice, and a literal `port` here fails the build. The SuperApp's reachable surface (the ADB-over-mesh plane and the DevControl loopback API) is reached through the nix door. A literal `bind` is used only where the owner's sshd_config is private. Nothing live is stored: state, banner, sessions and uptime are probed when the page asks.
ssh_doors._doc_mesh_only: MESH-ONLY (SSH reachable over the mesh VPN only), ON by default, PER PORT: every door has its own switch (power store: `mesh_only` for the nix door, `door_mesh_only.<id>` for the others; absent = the door's `mesh_only_default_on`, true). The switch is persisted here (power store key mesh_only; absent = the hosting app's declared default_on) and travels with every start signal; the hosting app binds the sshd to the WireGuard mesh addresses plus loopback, resolved at start from its live interfaces, and FAILS CLOSED (no sshd) when the mesh has no address. A change restarts a wanted door that is up on the new bind. The SSHd tab shows each door's OBSERVED listening addresses (from /proc/net where Android lets this app read it) as mesh-only or EXPOSED. Enforcement reaches the doors that have a hook (the nix door); Termux has none, so its badge is observation only.
ssh_doors._doc_authorized_keys: The webserver door's own authorized set (pubkey auth only, no password): the PUBLIC halves of the fleet's two deploy keys, exactly the lines of cloud-u-linux da__my-konsole/termux/authorized_keys that provision the nix and termux doors. The constellation ed25519 key is the one every app bakes from the vault; the ssh-rsa key is the fleet MCP's vault_id_rsa (cloud-superapp-mcp, `ssh -p 8025`). Public keys are not secrets. Baked here so this door does not depend on the nix terminal's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys; an optional authorized_keys file next to the power store adds to it. server/src/sshd.rs reads it.

doors.title: Cloud Terminal Nix
doors.note: Started and stopped by this app's keep-alive supervisor; the key list is the terminal's own ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.

doors.title: Cloud C3 Webserver
doors.bind: mesh addresses and loopback only while Mesh-only is ON
doors.note: Hosted by this app: ON by default, on its own port, supervised by this app's Keep alive and Server switches. Mesh-only has its own switch (default ON).

doors.title: Cloud Terminal Termux
doors.note: The sshd of Cloud Terminal Termux (our constellation-signed fleet app): its shell has fleet binder IPC like the nix and webserver shells. Started from that terminal; no start hook from here yet.

served._doc: The Pages tab (server/src/served.rs): ONE list of served pages, the add form and the undeclared-pages checker. `probe` is what the checker connects to on 127.0.0.1 besides /proc/net/tcp (which Android 10+ may hide): the fleet's own range and a few well-known dev ports. A TCP port that answers there and is in none of: serving.endpoints, every `port` under runtime, ssh_doors ports, the Repos store, the adopted ports, is UNDECLARED. Nothing outside the probe is claimed.

repos._doc: #1490 the Repos sub-page: the owner adds many entries, each (source, repo, start folder or entry file) with its OWN port and its own start/stop, so several sites serve at once. Persisted declaratively in `store` (JSON, one object per entry). Each site is a fleet-webserver on its own listener (the same one-folder, traversal-guarded, GET/HEAD-only serving as libs:local-serve, whose WebView page is Kotlin and so cannot live in this Rust-only app), bound to loopback or, when the entry says `mesh`, to the mesh address; never to a public one. `local` sources are read from disk under `root`; `terminal` sources are the terminals' own my-webserver (their $HOME), read through its loopback port and reached with a path-guarded GET proxy. Ports are allocated from port_first..port_last, outside every port the fleet declares (sshd 8023-8024 and the loopback servers 8000-8004 are below it).

direct._doc: #1615 the Git Sites sub-page (Pages > Git Sites, server/src/sub.rs::page_git): repositories offered for ONE-CLICK direct serving over this webserver, through the same repos.rs host / fleet-webserver render path as any repo site (md + html rendered, every other file downloadable, loopback or mesh only, never public). Each entry names a `source` declared under `sources` above and a `repo` (path/folder relative to that source). The Termux home git dir lives in another app's uid/home and is NOT resolvable from this app's process, so the Termux git-area repos are DECLARED here (configurable) rather than scanned; serving a `termux`/`nix` source still needs that terminal's own my-webserver answering. Local (emulated) git repos are additionally auto-discovered on the page.

roots._doc: #1677 the Pages tab roots (server/src/roots.rs): Pages > File Explorer shows each `explorer` root as a two-column explorer (tree left, the selected file rendered right); Pages > Pages serves each `pages` root like a browser (the folder's index, the first of `index` it holds, opens and its links navigate inside the root); Pages > All lists every root, each opening in its own mode. A root is a `source` of repos.sources (local: read from disk; terminal: that terminal's own my-webserver on loopback) and a `repo` folder relative to it (empty = the source's top). Files are served same-origin under /__app__/root/<id>/<path> through the repos serving paths (traversal-guarded, GET only). A missing clone is a 'clone it' state (`clone` is the command shown), a closed terminal offers Start app, missing storage access routes to Configs > Perms; nothing is an error screen.

explorer.label: Cloud Termux
explorer.note: Cloud Termux's ~/ (read through its own my-webserver)

adb_shell._doc: #1677 the bottom nav's ADB Shell tab opens the Cloud SuperApp's ADB Shell page (Configs > ADB Shell, its section page config/adb-shell): the SuperApp's launcher intent (serving.bridge_package) carrying the String extra `extra` = `value`, which the SuperApp's ShellActivity reads on create and on a new intent (handleShortcutIntent, page:<section>/<page> grammar). If the SuperApp is not installed the tab says so. Configs stays reachable from the top bar's gear (the fleet-default top-bar entry).
adb_shell.label: ADB Shell

serving._doc: THE ONE name -> port map of the phone's local servers, and the private DNS that names them. It holds NO port number: each endpoint names its `owner` (an app dir) and `port_from`, the path inside that owner's build.json where the port is declared (ac_cloud-termux and ac_cloud-nix-on-droid: runtime.webserver.port; this app: runtime.port and runtime.diag.port), and every reader resolves the number from there at BUILD time -- server/build.rs (the Rust crate: it compiles the resolved copy in, so src-tauri/build.rs and server/src/serving.rs see an ordinary `port`) and ac_cloud-browser/app/build.gradle (baked into the browser, which fails the build when its pinned tabs drift or an endpoint spells a literal `port`). A port number written here would be a second copy of the owner's, so test/test-c3-webserver-ports.sh fails on one. .app is a real public TLD and termux.app is a real website: only these four exact names are answered, by this app's own DNS server on loopback (udp, never :53 -- Android cannot bind it without root and cannot point the system resolver at loopback), and only our own apps ask it; nothing is changed system-wide. DNS carries no ports, so the browser maps the port from the resolved block. test/test-localhost-ports.sh fails when a port or name repeats across apps.

dns._doc_resolve: Each endpoint's `resolve` says how Cloud Browser finds its address: `declared` = straight from this block (the name is OWNED by the fleet and stands for `answer`, 127.0.0.1, so no DNS query is needed and a stopped server cannot break the lookup); `dns` = ask the DNS above (a dynamic name). The browser still needs the SERVER up: it starts keepalive when the endpoint's port does not accept a connection.
dns._doc: Loopback only, both the socket and the answer. 5354 because :53 needs root and 5353 is the mDNS port, held by Android's own mDNS daemon and the SuperApp's firestack (a bind there failed with Address already in use, and sharing it would misdeliver queries). Not a system resolver: it answers the four names below, says NODATA for other record types of them and REFUSES every other name; it never forwards.

endpoints.name: termux.app
endpoints.title: Termux
endpoints.summary: Cloud Terminal Termux's $HOME, served by its own my-webserver

endpoints.name: nix.app
endpoints.title: Nix
endpoints.summary: Cloud Terminal Nix-on-Droid's $HOME, served by its own my-webserver

endpoints.name: emulated.app
endpoints.title: Local
endpoints.summary: The emulated drive, /storage/emulated/0, and nothing else

endpoints.name: cloud.app
endpoints.title: X-Ray Device
endpoints.summary: X-Ray Device profile: the SuperApp's device scan (device/OS, perms, storage, battery, memory/CPU, the stack sections), with Logcat and Diagnose. Served on cloud.app:8003 (id and DNS name kept stable).

keepalive._doc: The persistent foreground service that keeps this app's servers (drive, diagnostics, private DNS) bound without the UI: started at boot and after an update (BootReceiver), by the activity, and by Cloud Browser when a private name's server does not answer (explicit intent by package and class; the service is exported behind the fleet's CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission, so only a fleet-signed app can start it). START_STICKY restarts it if the system kills it. Read by app/build.gradle of the browser, which bakes it as ui.browser.private_names.service and the package into its <queries>.

opener._doc: A served page is handed to this app as an explicit-package VIEW intent by the diagnostics bridge's opener; it is never offered to any other browser, because a private name sent to the system would resolve on the public internet.

bridge._doc: The SuperApp's exported, CONSTELLATION_DATA signature-permission ContentProvider (aa_cloud-superapp FleetDiagnosticsProvider). call(about|logcat|diagnose) -> {ok, mime, payload}; read-only.

render_engines._doc: THE ENGINE REGISTRY, declared once: every render and feature engine of the web server this app runs. Since the :8002 UI became the shared fleet-webserver, these are the SHARED server's engines (the Linux my-webserver feature set): Configs > Engines draws exactly this list, read-only, because the shared server has no per-engine switch. server/src/engines.rs compiles this block in; a test holds ids unique and every row described. group render|feature are what the server does to a file or request, core is what every request relies on, not-portable is an engine of my-webserver that is not served here and says why (reason).

list.name: Markdown
list.summary: marked.js 15 draws the file as a GitHub-dark page with a breadcrumb and a view-raw link; ?raw sends the source.

list.name: JSON viewer
list.summary: Objects become key/value tables, arrays of objects sortable tables, nested values cards; row filter, collapsible sections, copy buttons.

list.name: YAML viewer
list.summary: js-yaml 4.1 parses the file and the same tables draw it; a parse error falls back to the raw text.

list.name: Secrets table
list.summary: Key/value rows with a copy button per row and a red badge. Nothing is decrypted here: the file is shown as stored.

list.name: Eruda DevTools
list.summary: Injects the bundled Eruda 3.4.3 console, elements and network panels into HTML, index pages and rendered pages. No CDN.

list.name: HTML pages
list.summary: Serves .html natively, opens a directory's index.html with a <base>, and /route falls back to route.html.

list.name: SPA fallback
list.summary: An unknown path inside a prerendered SvelteKit project serves its nearest ancestor 200.html with root-absolute assets rewritten.

list.name: File browser
list.summary: Sidebar tree, breadcrumb path bar, a viewer pane with a raw/rendered switch and a copy-raw button: the Linux frontend, byte for byte.

list.name: Search
list.summary: Folder, filename and content search. Breadth-first, bounded by 3 s, 50 000 entries and 200 results, and says when it stopped early.

list.name: Hidden files
list.summary: Lists and searches dot entries when asked (the Dot files switch).

list.name: Preview
list.summary: Returns a text file (at most 5 MB) as JSON for the viewer pane.

list.name: Fleet diagnostics bridge
list.summary: About, Logcat and Diagnose of the SuperApp, read through its signature-permission provider.

list.name: Directory listing
list.summary: Folders first, then files by name, dangling symlinks shown as broken links instead of vanishing.

list.name: Static files
list.summary: MIME table with text sniffing for unknown types, ?raw plain-text passthrough, HEAD.

list.name: Root confinement
list.summary: Each path is canonicalised and must stay inside the served root; .. and symlinks that leave it are 404.

list.name: Loopback only
list.summary: Binds 127.0.0.1 and refuses any other peer. GET and HEAD only; the single POSTs are the app's own guarded link opener and the shared write API (off).

list.name: Private DNS
list.summary: Answers the four private .app names declared in build.json with 127.0.0.1 and refuses every other name. Only our own apps ask it; the system never does.

list.name: Open in cloud-browser
list.summary: Any link the web server serves, and every served page of the Pages tab, can be handed to cloud-browser from the link chooser (Open in browser).

list.name: Write API
list.summary: Writes a file under an allow-listed directory with a shared-secret token (loopback only, off unless the environment turns it on).
list.reason: This app does not turn it on: it needs a provisioned token file and is a write path into shared storage; the app is read-only by design.

list.name: Git push API
list.summary: add, commit and push a scoped set of paths.
list.reason: Needs a git binary and credentials the app does not have, and an exec surface a Tauri app does not carry.

list.name: Watchdog snapshot
list.summary: Hands over my-watchdog's two-second metrics file.
list.reason: The snapshot lives in /run or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR of a Linux session; Android has neither, and the phone's metrics are the Home tab.

list.name: App panels
list.summary: Serves another project's dist/ directory as a panel.
list.reason: Resolves a checkout under $HOME/git; there is no such tree on the phone.

links._doc: THE LINK-OPEN DECLARATION. Every link the web server serves (in the file view, in rendered pages, in listings, in the Pages tab) is classified by the first `types` row whose `schemes` and `hosts` match it, and the type names the choices the link chooser offers; nothing in server/ui/shell.html spells a type or a choice. hosts: local = loopback and the four private .app names (they resolve only through this app's private DNS, so Open embedded rewrites them to 127.0.0.1:<port>), external = anything else, any = both. A choice is `browser` (hand the URL to cloud-browser, explicit-package VIEW intent) or `embedded` (open it inside this app's WebView, so the system back gesture follows the WebView history, then falls back to the app). `remember` offers a per-type 'Remember my choice' tick; the stored choice lives in the app WebView's localStorage and Configs > Links resets it. A type with one choice does not ask.

android._doc_application_id: Identity, not brand (#405/#495): the package id stays through the rename to cloud-c3-webserver, exactly as ac_c3-watchdog keeps com.diegonmarcos.watchdog, because moving it forces a manual reinstall on every phone.
android._doc_target_sdk: 28 for the STORAGE model: at 28 one READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE grant (asked by libs:perms' first run and Configs > Perms, #1682; the Tauri host asked it from Rust) covers the whole of runtime.serve_root; from 29 scoped storage would need MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE or per-tree grants to serve shared storage. compile_sdk is what the app and the shared libs compile against.
android._doc_gradle_module: The native app's module (its Tauri-era path, kept because other apps read its AndroidManifest.xml there); aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T6 reads it to check the launcher label is build.json::name.

adb_owner_modules._doc: #1682 P2b the ADB owner side's libs, included by src-tauri/gen/android/settings.gradle (dir = the shared libs root + the lib name; no literal path, so the shipped build's lib closure does not count them) ONLY when 1_cicd/src/data/adb-owner.json names this app (or the non-shipped CI verify sets C3_ADB_OWNER_VERIFY=1). Not in `modules`: the shipped build links none of them while the SuperApp owns ADB (test-shell-broker-guards.sh B1/B11).

modules._doc: Shared modules the gradle project (native.android_project) includes BY REFERENCE beside :app. Its settings.gradle iterates this map and, like every other reader of it (the ship workflow's trigger derivation, the publish gate, ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/shared-modules.test.sh), resolves each dir against THIS directory, not against the gradle root three levels down. They are compiled Kotlin libraries, not source in this app's tree, so test/test-c3-webserver-native.sh (K2) does not see them. libs:devtools finds this file by walking up from the gradle root (src-tauri/gen/android), as libs:analytics does, so there is one declaration and no copy.

libs:fleet-notify.comment: #1660 FleetNotify + KeepAliveStatus (the keep-alive and data-widget notifications), out of libs:core; linked by the app (the servers keep-alive notification).

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership: core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission (defined and requested). Declared so a core change rebuilds this app instead of shipping a stale mesh member.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>); not linked directly. Listed so its changes also trigger a rebuild, and because Gradle resolves core's project path against this app's settings.gradle.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:ui-icons._doc: libs:bottomnav's dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

toolchain._doc: Pinned here, read by the ship workflow and mirrored in flake.nix. agp/gradle/kotlin are the gradle project's (src-tauri/gen/android/build.gradle.kts, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties); gradle itself comes from the committed wrapper. #1682: no tauri CLI any more; the Rust core is a plain cargo build with the NDK clang as linker.
toolchain._doc_rust: Stable channel, no nightly feature. The ship workflow installs it through dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with the Android targets native.targets names.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps, resolved by build.sh::_resolve_signing from the vault. No fallback key.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution, same data-driven block as every app here; build.sh oras-push and gh-release read it.

variants._doc: supported_abis is exactly the one ABI each APK's binary is built for: an aarch64 static executable cannot start on a 32-bit-only phone.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. The server crate's own suite (cargo test) and the SHARED web server's suite (ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/fleet-webserver: vendor hash == the cloud-u-linux copy, every endpoint's contract, parity against the real Linux server) execute in the ship workflow's build job before the APK is built.

shell._doc_requires: node runs the Linux my-webserver as the oracle and the render check drives headless Chrome at the A37 density. A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail, it answers from the tool's absence, so a missing one is fatal at the engine's preflight.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: The phone's own web server and crash sink
about.description: Cloud C3 WebServer runs the fleet's shared web server on the phone, as a native Kotlin / Compose app over a Rust core (#1682). It serves the fleet web UI on port 8002, browses shared storage under /storage/emulated/0 and nothing else, and is the local crash sink every other fleet app posts its crash reports to over loopback. It exists so crash reports never leave the phone unless the owner shares them, and so the desktop's web UI is also available on the phone, offline.
features: Fleet web UI served on the phone (port 8002)
Local crash sink for every fleet app
Crash list of every fleet app, readable in a browser

screens.name: Home
screens.what: The fleet web UI served on port 8002.

screens.name: SSHd
screens.what: Every fleet SSH door with live state and Start / Stop, and below it the shared storage file view (read-only browsing).

screens.name: Crashes
screens.what: Crash reports posted by the fleet's apps.

guide: Open the app once so the server starts.
Visit http://127.0.0.1:8002 in Cloud Browser to use the web UI.
Open the Crashes page after an app crashed to read its report.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

perms_why.write_settings: Parity grant with the SuperApp (perms.needs): backs the user-controllable system-settings plane (screen brightness, auto-rotate, timeout) that the X-Ray Device page's device profile reports on; the write itself is performed by the SuperApp service this Rust app mirrors, not by this app directly.
perms_why.dnd_access: Parity grant with the SuperApp (perms.needs): lets the X-Ray Device page's device profile read the Do Not Disturb / notification-policy state the device scan reports; the policy change is performed by the SuperApp service this Rust app mirrors, not by this app directly.

related.why: Opens the web UI this app serves.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
perms._doc_parity: PERMISSIONS PARITY with aa_cloud-superapp (owner decision): needs is the SuperApp's perms.needs plus this app's own storage_read. Not carried, because each is bound to a Kotlin service class the SuperApp owns and this app does not carry (#1682 made it native Kotlin; adding such a service is its own decision): notification_listener, accessibility, device_admin, vpn. write_secure_settings supersedes #1515, which kept it on the SuperApp alone; it is pm-granted per app, and the SuperApp keeps its grant. test/test-c3-webserver-perms-parity.sh holds the manifest and this list to the SuperApp's.
